title: Infection Control for the PCP: PPE, Sharps and Exposures
next: Chapter 39, Lesson 2: Sepsis, key infectious diseases, and a clean ambulance

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already wear gloves, wash your hands and wipe down the stretcher. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Match your PPE to the route a disease spreads by
  2. Handle your new sharps, IV catheters, safely
  3. Know the exact steps after a needlestick or splash

Textbook: Chapter 39, PDF pages 3317–3345
slides.say: Welcome back. As EMRs, you already practise infection control every shift. You wear gloves, you wash your hands, and you clean the stretcher after each call. So why a whole lesson on it now? Because your job as a PCP puts you closer to blood and to the airway. You'll start IVs with needles that have been inside a vein, and you'll use breathing treatments that can spray germs into the air. Today we'll cover three things: how to choose protective equipment based on how a disease spreads, how to handle your new sharps safely, and exactly what to do if you're stuck by a needle or splashed with blood.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。作为 EMR，你们每个班都在做感染防控：戴手套、洗手、每趟出车后清洁担架。那为什么现在还要专门讲一节？因为 PCP 的工作让你更靠近血液和气道。你要用在静脉里待过的针开静脉，还要做可能把病菌喷到空气中的呼吸治疗。今天讲三件事：怎样按疾病的传播途径选择防护装备；怎样安全处理你新多出来的锐器；被针扎或被血溅到之后具体该怎么做。

slides.title: How diseases spread: five routes
slides.body:
RouteHow it travelsExamples
AirborneTiny particles float and are inhaledTB, measles, chickenpox
DropletHeavy drops fall within 1–2 mInfluenza, mumps, meningococcal meningitis
ContactHands or equipment carry germs to broken skin, eyes, nose, mouthPink eye, C. difficile
VehicleContaminated food, water or bloodHepatitis A and B, Salmonella
VectorBite of a mosquito, tick or animalWest Nile virus, malaria
slides.say: First question on every call: how does this germ travel? There are five routes. Airborne germs are so tiny they float in the air and get breathed in. Only three common diseases spread this way between people: TB, measles, and chickenpox. Droplets are heavier. They come out with a cough or a sneeze and fall within one to two metres. Contact spread happens when hands or equipment carry germs to broken skin, or to the eyes, nose, or mouth. Vehicle spread is through contaminated food, water, or blood. And vector-borne diseases, like West Nile virus, need a mosquito or tick bite, so you can't catch them from your patient.
slides.sayZh: 每次出车的第一个问题：这种病菌怎么传播？途径有五种。空气传播的病原极小，能飘在空气里被吸入；以这种方式人传人的常见病只有三种：结核、麻疹、水痘。飞沫比较重，随咳嗽或喷嚏喷出，一到两米内就落地。接触传播是手或器械把病菌带到破损皮肤或眼、鼻、口。媒介物传播经被污染的食物、水或血液。虫媒病，比如西尼罗病毒，需要蚊或蜱叮咬，所以你不会从病人身上直接染上。

slides.title: Exposure is not infection
slides.body:
Exposure ≠ infection

  • Dose: how many germs got in
  • Virulence: how strong they are, how long they last outside
  • Mode of entry: the right door (a respiratory virus in a cut usually won't infect)
  • Host resistance: your health and your vaccines

Some diseases spread before symptoms start, so protect yourself on every call.
slides.say: Being exposed does not mean you will get sick. Four things decide your real risk. The dose: some germs need millions to cause illness, others only a few hundred. Virulence: how strong the germ is and how long it survives outside the body. HIV, for example, dies quickly in air and light. The mode of entry: a respiratory virus in a cut usually won't infect you, but breathed in, it can. That's why a mask on a coughing patient works so well. And your own resistance, built by good health and vaccines. Remember, some diseases spread before any symptoms appear.
slides.sayZh: 暴露不等于会生病。真正的风险由四个因素决定。剂量：有的病菌要上百万个才致病，有的几百个就够。毒力：病菌有多强、离开人体后能活多久；比如 HIV 遇到空气和光很快就死。侵入途径：呼吸道病毒落进伤口通常不会感染你，但吸进去就可能，所以给咳嗽的病人戴口罩特别有效。还有你自己的抵抗力，靠健康和疫苗来增强。记住，有些病在出现任何症状之前就能传染。

slides.title: Routine practices: every patient
slides.body:
Health Canada's standard since 1999: act on signs and route, not on the diagnosis.

  • Hand hygiene and PPE
  • Sharps safety
  • Patient placement during transport
  • Routine equipment cleaning
  • Vehicle cleaning after every patient
Intact skin→PPE→Post-exposure follow-up
slides.say: In Canada, the standard is called routine practices, introduced by Health Canada in 1999. You don't wait for a diagnosis. You protect yourself based on the signs you see and how the disease could spread, and you do it for every patient, because anyone could be infectious. The six parts are hand hygiene, PPE, sharps safety, careful patient placement during transport, routine equipment cleaning, and cleaning the vehicle after every patient. Think of three lines of defence: your intact skin first, PPE second, and post-exposure follow-up, meaning medical care after an exposure, third.
slides.sayZh: 在加拿大，这套标准叫常规防护，由加拿大卫生部在 1999 年推出。不等诊断，而是根据看到的症状和可能的传播途径来防护，而且对每位病人都这样做，因为任何人都可能有传染性。六个部分是：手卫生、个人防护装备、锐器安全、转运时合理安置病人、器械常规清洁、每位病人之后清洁车辆。把防护想成三道防线：完整的皮肤是第一道，PPE 是第二道，暴露后随访——也就是暴露之后的医疗处理——是第三道。

slides.title: Hand hygiene: the most important step
slides.body:
Hand washing is the single most important way to prevent infection

  • Rub for at least 20 seconds, then rinse well
  • Alcohol gel is fine, but not for visibly dirty hands
  • C. difficile spores: soap and water only
  • Never gel your gloves; wash after you take them off
  • Cover cuts; if you can't, skip high-risk procedures
slides.say: Health Canada calls hand washing the single most important way to prevent infection. Use warm water and enough soap, and rub hard for at least twenty seconds. Alcohol gel is fine for clean hands, but not when hands are visibly dirty. Alcohol also can't remove spores, so if you suspect C. difficile, a germ that causes severe diarrhea, use soap and water. Gloves don't replace hand washing: they can have tiny holes, so wash after removing them, and never put sanitizer on gloves, because it breaks them down. Finally, cover cuts on your hands. If a wound is too big to cover, avoid high-risk procedures such as IV starts.
slides.sayZh: 加拿大卫生部说，洗手是预防感染最重要的一项措施。用温水和足量皂液，用力搓至少二十秒。手干净时用酒精洗手液可以，但手上看得见脏就不行。酒精也去不掉芽孢，所以怀疑艰难梭菌——一种引起严重腹泻的细菌——时，要用肥皂和流水。手套不能代替洗手：手套可能有微小破洞，摘下后要洗手；也绝不要往手套上抹洗手液，会损坏手套。最后，手上的伤口要包好；伤口太大盖不住，就不要做开静脉这类高风险操作。

slides.q: A man has coughed for four weeks, with night sweats and weight loss. What respiratory protection is right?
options: A surgical mask on you is enough
A fit-tested N95 on you, and a surgical mask on him
None, because TB is not very contagious
A surgical mask on him only; you need nothing
slides.say: Time for a question. A man has had a cough for four weeks, with night sweats and weight loss. What respiratory protection is right? A, a surgical mask on you is enough. B, a fit-tested N95 on you, and a surgical mask on him. C, none, because TB is not very contagious. D, a surgical mask on him only; you need nothing. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一道题。一名男子咳嗽四周，伴盗汗和体重下降。哪种呼吸防护是对的？A，你戴外科口罩就够了；B，你戴经过适合性测试的 N95，给他戴外科口罩；C，不用防护，因为结核传染性不强；D，只给他戴外科口罩，你不用戴。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A cough longer than three weeks with night sweats and weight loss suggests TB, which is airborne. A fit-tested N95 filters the air you breathe in, and a surgical mask on the patient catches what he breathes out. A is wrong because a surgical mask mainly blocks splashes. C is a trap: TB isn't highly contagious, but airborne spread still needs a respirator. D leaves you unprotected.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。咳嗽超过三周加盗汗和消瘦提示结核，而结核经空气传播。经过适合性测试的 N95 过滤你吸进的空气，病人戴的外科口罩拦住他呼出的东西。A 错，外科口罩主要挡飞溅。C 是陷阱：结核传染性确实不强，但空气传播仍然需要呼吸器。D 让你自己毫无防护。

slides.title: Matching PPE to the route
slides.body:
RouteOn the patientOn you
AirborneSurgical maskFit-tested N95
DropletSurgical maskSurgical mask or N95, eye protection, gloves
Contact—Gloves; gown if your uniform may get soiled
Blood—Gloves, eye protection; gown for big splashes

Fever + rash? Put a surgical mask on the patient first.
slides.say: Now let's match PPE to the route. For airborne diseases, put a surgical mask on the patient and a fit-tested N95 on yourself. Fit-testing matters, because a respirator that doesn't seal gives false confidence; repeat it after a big weight change. For droplet diseases like influenza, the patient wears a surgical mask, and you wear a surgical mask or N95, eye protection, and gloves. For contact spread, use gloves, plus a gown if your uniform could touch drainage. For blood, wear gloves and eye protection, and a gown for big splashes, like a birth or heavy bleeding. And any patient with fever and a rash gets a surgical mask.
slides.sayZh: 现在按途径匹配 PPE。空气传播病：给病人戴外科口罩，你自己戴经过适合性测试的 N95。适合性测试很重要，因为密封不好的呼吸器只会给你虚假的安全感；体重变化大之后要重测。飞沫传播病，比如流感：病人戴外科口罩，你戴外科口罩或 N95、护目镜和手套。接触传播：戴手套，制服可能碰到引流液时加穿隔离衣。血液：戴手套和护目镜，遇到大量飞溅，比如分娩或大出血，要穿隔离衣。还有，发热加皮疹的病人一律戴外科口罩。

slides.title: Putting PPE on and taking it off
slides.body:
On:

Gown→N95→Eye protection→Gloves

Off (dirtiest first):

Gloves→Gown→Eye protection→N95
  • Taking PPE off is when you contaminate yourself
  • Gel your hands between steps if needed
  • Driver's seat: no PPE except a respirator and eyewear
slides.say: The order matters. To put PPE on: gown, then the N95, then eye protection, and gloves last. To take it off: gloves first, because they are the dirtiest, then the gown, then eye protection, and the N95 last. Notice it's not simply the reverse. Taking PPE off is the moment you're most likely to contaminate yourself, so go slowly, don't touch clean skin or clothes, and use alcohol gel between steps whenever you need to. One more rule: no gloves or gown in the driver's compartment, or you'll contaminate the steering wheel and radio. A respirator and eye protection are the exceptions.
slides.sayZh: 顺序很重要。穿：先隔离衣，再 N95，再护目镜，最后手套。脱：先脱手套，因为它最脏；再隔离衣，再护目镜，最后 N95。注意，这不是简单地倒过来。脱 PPE 时最容易污染自己，所以动作放慢，别碰干净的皮肤或衣服，需要时在每一步之间用酒精洗手液擦手。还有一条：手套和隔离衣不能穿进驾驶室，否则会污染方向盘和对讲机；呼吸器和护目镜是例外。

slides.title: Sharps safety with IV starts
slides.body:
• Say "sharps out" and "sharps clear"; count your sharps
  • Into the sharps box right away, even safety devices
  • Never recap, bend, break, pocket or pass a needle
  • Never leave a sharp for someone else
  • Use safety catheters and needleless systems
  • Change the container at the full line

Needlesticks are the top cause of bloodborne infection in health care: about 50,000 a year in Canadian hospitals.
slides.say: As a PCP, you'll handle a new kind of sharp: the IV catheter. Needlesticks are the most common cause of bloodborne infection in health care, about fifty thousand a year in Canadian hospitals. So build these habits now. Call out 'sharps out' and 'sharps clear', so your partner stays back. Count your sharps, and drop each one into the sharps container the moment you're done, even safety devices that retract. Never recap, bend, or break a needle, never pocket one, and never pass an exposed sharp or leave it for your partner. And change the container at the full line, not when it's overflowing.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，你要处理一种新的锐器：静脉留置针。针刺伤是医疗场所血源性感染最常见的原因，加拿大医院每年约五万例。所以现在就养成这些习惯：喊出「锐器出」和「锐器清」，让搭档避开。清点锐器，用完立刻丢进锐器盒，就算是会自动回缩的安全针也一样。绝不回帽、不折弯、不掰断针头，绝不放进口袋，绝不递出裸露的锐器，也不留给搭档收拾。锐器盒到满线就换，别等到溢出来。

slides.title: What makes a needlestick high-risk
slides.body:
The book's high-risk features:

  • A deep puncture
  • Visible blood on the device
  • The device was in a vein or artery
  • A hollow-bore, large-gauge needle
  • A source patient with a high viral load

An IV catheter needle ticks most of these boxes. Tears, sweat, urine, vomit and sputum don't spread bloodborne disease unless they contain visible blood.
slides.say: Not all exposures are equal. The book lists the high-risk features: a deep puncture, visible blood on the device, a device that was in a vein or artery, a hollow-bore needle, meaning one with a hollow centre that holds blood, and a source patient with a high viral load, meaning lots of virus in the blood. Now picture an IV catheter needle just after you enter the vein: hollow, in a vein, and bloody. That's the high-risk profile, and it's new for you, because EMRs in BC don't start IVs. By contrast, tears, sweat, urine, stool, vomit, and sputum don't spread bloodborne disease unless they contain visible blood.
slides.sayZh: 暴露不都一样。书里列出高风险特征：刺得深；器械上看得见血；器械曾在静脉或动脉里；空心针，也就是中间有腔、能装血的针；以及源患者病毒载量高，即血中病毒很多。想象你刚刺入静脉后的留置针针芯：中空、在血管里待过、带着血——这正是高风险的样子，而且对你是新的，因为 BC 的 EMR 不开静脉。相比之下，眼泪、汗、尿、粪便、呕吐物和痰不传播血源性疾病，除非里面有肉眼可见的血。

slides.title: After an exposure: the steps
slides.body:
1. Tell your supervisor right away
  2. Go to the emergency department promptly
  3. Testing starts with the source patient: HIV, hepatitis B, rapid hepatitis C
  4. Counselling and treatment begin within 24–48 hours

Preventive treatment exists for many diseases, but not hepatitis C, which can often be cured.
slides.say: What counts as an exposure? A stick with a used needle, blood or other infectious fluid splashed into your eyes, nose, or mouth, blood on broken skin, a cut from a bloody sharp, or a human bite that draws blood. In a bite, the source is the person who is bleeding. If it happens, tell your supervisor right away and get to the emergency department promptly. Testing starts with the source patient, not with you: HIV, hepatitis B, and a rapid hepatitis C test. Counselling and treatment should begin within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. Preventive treatment exists for many diseases, but not for hepatitis C, which can often be cured.
slides.sayZh: 什么算暴露？被用过的针扎到；血或其他感染性体液溅进眼、鼻、口；血沾到破损皮肤；被带血的锐器割伤；或被人咬伤且见血——咬伤时，源头是流血的那个人。一旦发生，立刻报告上级，尽快去急诊。检测从源患者开始，而不是从你开始：查 HIV、乙肝，并做快速丙肝检测。咨询和治疗应在二十四到四十八小时内开始。很多病都有暴露后的预防性治疗，但丙肝没有；不过丙肝常常可以治愈。

slides.q: En route, the IV catheter needle you just pulled from a vein punctures your glove and finger. What should you do?
options: Keep working, and report it only if you feel unwell later
Tell your supervisor and get assessed at the emergency department promptly
Wait four to six weeks, then get your own blood tested
Recap the needle so no one else gets hurt, then carry on
slides.say: Here's a PCP situation. En route, the IV catheter needle you just pulled out of a vein punctures your glove and your finger. What should you do? A, keep working, and report it only if you feel unwell later. B, tell your supervisor and get assessed at the emergency department promptly. C, wait four to six weeks, then get your own blood tested. D, recap the needle so no one else gets hurt, then carry on. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一个 PCP 场景。转运途中，你刚从静脉拔出的留置针针芯扎穿手套刺进手指。你该怎么做？A，继续工作，以后觉得不舒服再报告；B，报告上级，尽快去急诊评估；C，等四到六周再去查自己的血；D，先给针回帽免得别人受伤，然后继续工作。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. This is a high-risk exposure: a hollow needle, fresh from a vein, with blood on it. Report it and get to the emergency department promptly, so source testing can start and any treatment begins within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. A wastes the window for preventive treatment. C skips the source patient, where testing begins. D is wrong because you never recap; the needle goes straight into the sharps container.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。这是高风险暴露：空心针、刚从静脉出来、带着血。要报告并尽快去急诊，好让源患者检测尽早开始，任何治疗都能在二十四到四十八小时内启动。A 会错过预防性治疗的时机。C 跳过了源患者，而检测从源患者开始。D 错，绝不回帽，针头应直接丢进锐器盒。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: new skills, new exposures
slides.body:
All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Routine practices, hand hygiene, cleaning
  • Salbutamol by MDI or nebulizer
  • Flu-like illness: MDI + spacer strongly recommended
  • BVM ventilation and suction
  • IM epinephrine, naloxone, glucagon

PCP adds

  • IV access, with aseptic technique
  • IV naloxone and D10W
  • CPAP, and PEEP on the BVM
  • Salbutamol + ipratropium nebulizer
  • Supraglottic airway in cardiac arrest

BC protocols: IV Procedures, SOB (Asthma/COPD), CPAP, Diabetic, Narcotic Overdose, CPR
slides.say: Let's compare the licence levels and see where the exposure risk sits. Everyone, EMR and PCP, uses routine practices, gives salbutamol, ventilates with a bag-valve mask, suctions, and gives some IM injections, like epinephrine, naloxone, and glucagon. Notice one BC detail: for a patient with a flu-like illness, BC strongly recommends salbutamol by MDI and spacer. Now the PCP column. You add IV access, and BC says to keep aseptic technique throughout. You add IV naloxone and D10W, CPAP, PEEP, the salbutamol and ipratropium nebulizer, and a supraglottic airway in cardiac arrest. Every one of these puts you closer to blood or to aerosols, so your PPE has to step up too.
slides.sayZh: 来比一比各级别，看暴露风险在哪里。所有人——EMR 和 PCP——都执行常规防护、给沙丁胺醇、用球囊面罩通气、吸引，还会做一些肌注，比如肾上腺素、纳洛酮、胰高血糖素。注意一个 BC 细节：病人有流感样症状时，BC 强烈建议用 MDI 加储雾罐给沙丁胺醇。再看 PCP 这一栏：你多了静脉通路，BC 要求全程无菌操作；还多了静脉给纳洛酮和 D10W、CPAP、PEEP、沙丁胺醇加异丙托溴铵雾化，以及心脏骤停时的声门上气道。每一项都让你更靠近血液或气溶胶，所以你的防护也要跟着升级。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• IV catheter needles: hollow, in a vein, bloody; your riskiest sharp
  • En route IVs: keep a sharps container within reach
  • Rough road? Ask your partner to stop briefly
  • CPAP, nebulizers: N95 + eyewear for coughing, feverish patients
  • A cut you can't cover: no high-risk procedures
  • Any exposure: report it right away
slides.say: Here are the new risks to watch for. Your riskiest sharp is now the IV catheter needle: hollow, in a vein, and bloody. Many BC protocols place the IV en route, and the textbook warns that needles in a moving ambulance are dangerous. So keep a sharps container within arm's reach, and on a rough road, ask your partner to stop briefly while you start the line. CPAP and nebulizers can push germs into the air, so for a coughing or feverish patient, wear an N95 and eye protection. With a cut you can't cover, skip high-risk procedures. And report any exposure right away.
slides.sayZh: 要注意的新风险：你最危险的锐器变成了静脉留置针针芯——中空、在血管里、带着血。BC 很多流程把开静脉放在转运途中，而教材提醒，在行驶的救护车里用针很危险。所以锐器盒要放在伸手可及处，路面颠簸时请搭档短暂停车再开静脉。CPAP 和雾化会把病菌推进空气里，所以面对咳嗽或发热的病人要戴 N95 和护目镜。手上有盖不住的伤口，就别做高风险操作。一旦暴露，马上报告。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Match PPE to the route: N95 for TB, measles, chickenpox; mask the patient
  2. IV needles are high-risk sharps: never recap, dispose at once
  3. Exposure: report, go to the ED, source testing first, treatment within 24–48 h

Next: sepsis, key infectious diseases, and a clean ambulance
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: match your PPE to the route. TB, measles, and chickenpox are the airborne three, so wear a fit-tested N95, and mask any coughing patient, or anyone with fever and a rash. Two: your IV catheter needle is a high-risk sharp. Call it out, never recap it, and drop it in the sharps container right away. Three: after an exposure, report it and go to the emergency department; testing starts with the source patient, and treatment begins within twenty-four to forty-eight hours. Next lesson: sepsis, the key diseases, and a clean ambulance. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，按传播途径选 PPE：结核、麻疹、水痘是空气传播三病，要戴经过适合性测试的 N95；给咳嗽的病人、或发热加皮疹的病人戴口罩。二，静脉留置针针芯是高风险锐器：喊出来、绝不回帽、立刻丢进锐器盒。三，暴露后：报告并去急诊；检测从源患者开始，治疗在二十四到四十八小时内启动。下节课讲脓毒症、重点传染病和救护车清洁。下节课见。
